comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Second instance, and a more consequential one than the unit test this ticket was filed for: gate
congestion **refused a ticket CLOSE**, not just a test.

Attempting to close `2ba3-bf77-1303-4b2d` (epic 6202 S4, change 2659 already merged):

```
GATE_CONGESTED {"event":"GATE_CONGESTED","gate":"verify_completion",
                "ticket_id":"2ba3-bf77-1303-4b2d","limit":4}
Error: cannot close 2ba3-bf77-1303-4b2d: completion verification could not run
  (gate admission refused: all 4 concurrent gate slot(s) on this host are in use,
   so verify_completion was not started. This is HOST CONGESTION, not a review result —
   no verdict was produced and nothing about the ticket was judged. Retry later, or
   raise [snapshot].max_concurrent_gates if the host has room.)
```

## The cause was me, and I am recording that rather than filing it as someone else's problem

I had just run two `review-plan` gates back to back (`fd2b-7af3`, `eebc-6aa1`) to earn attestations
for a blocked change, while several dispatched agents were independently running their own plan
reviews. Four slots, more than four consumers. The host was simultaneously at **load average
39-44 on 18 cores with 40 concurrent pytest processes**, two of them full `make verify` runs — one
mine, one from another session's worktree (`janitor-a691-shims`).

So both instances of this ticket trace to the same thing: **an orchestrator fanning out more
concurrent work than the host's gate admission and CPU can carry.** That is a scheduling defect on
my side, not only a test-isolation defect in the code.

## What the gate did RIGHT, which is worth stating on a ticket about a failure

The refusal is exemplary and should not be "fixed" away. It says, in its own words, *"This is HOST
CONGESTION, not a review result — no verdict was produced and nothing about the ticket was
judged."* It refused to let an infrastructure limit masquerade as a verdict, named the remedy, and
distinguished itself from a real FAIL.

That is the exact opposite of the defect class this session has spent the night cataloguing — a
check reporting a judgement it never made. If `verify_completion` had instead returned a FAIL, or
silently passed, a merged story would have been mis-closed or wrongly held. Whatever remediation
this ticket produces, preserve that distinction.

It also offers `--force="<reason>"` as an override. I did not use it, and an automated retry with
backoff was the correct response: the operation was not judged, so there is nothing to override —
only something to wait for.

## Bearing on the fix

The originally-filed shape (a unit test taking a host-wide admission slot) is real and worth
fixing. But this instance shows the slot limit is also reachable by ordinary concurrent operation,
with no test involved. A fix that only stops tests from taking slots would not have prevented this
close from being refused. Worth deciding whether `[snapshot].max_concurrent_gates` is simply sized
for a quieter host than this one has become.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
## Root cause found, and it is much bigger than the single test I filed this for

I originally filed this from ONE failure during a `make verify`. A second full `make verify` on
the same host produced **twelve**, and the mechanism is now reproducible without any other
session running.

### The twelve

10 fail directly with `GateCongestedError: gate admission refused: all 4 concurrent slots busy`:

```
tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py::test_review_plan_preflight_tolerates_unrelated_untracked_tracker_files
tests/unit/test_plan_review_retry.py::test_retry_fails_closed_when_current_code_sha_is_uncomputable
tests/unit/test_plan_review_retry.py::test_retry_refuses_on_verified_at_sha_mismatch
tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py::test_material_change_reruns_full_review
tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py::test_code_change_reruns_full_review
tests/unit/test_gate_peak_rss_9ea3.py::test_both_gate_entry_points_emit_the_marker[review_plan-plan_review]
tests/unit/test_gate_peak_rss_9ea3.py::test_both_gate_entry_points_emit_the_marker[verify_completion-verify_completion]
tests/unit/workflow/test_gate_error_sidecar.py::test_plan_review_outage_writes_gate_error_and_still_degrades
tests/unit/workflow/test_gate_error_sidecar_heldout.py::test_existing_verdict_readers_skip_gate_error_record
tests/unit/workflow/test_gate_error_sidecar_heldout.py::test_gate_error_verdict_not_coerced_to_fail
```

2 more fail DOWNSTREAM of the same congestion, with a retry-count assertion rather than the
error itself — worth noting because they do not name the cause and would be misdiagnosed:

```
tests/unit/test_plan_review_cli_retry.py::test_cli_retry_refuses_unreviewed_ticket_with_zero_calls  - AssertionError: assert 11 == 2
tests/unit/test_plan_review_cli_retry.py::test_cli_retry_is_compatible_with_no_sign                 - AssertionError: assert 11 == 2
```

(The first `make verify` also caught
`tests/unit/test_completion_wrapper_duration_instrumentation.py::test_verify_completion_partitions_attempt_without_changing_verdict`,
the one this ticket was opened for, so the family is at least thirteen.)

### Deterministic reproduction — it is NOT other sessions, the suite races itself

Running just those twelve, with nothing else on the host:

```
serially            -> 12 passed in 152.57s
-n 4 (run 1)        ->  3 failed, 9 passed
-n 4 (run 2)        ->  4 failed, 8 passed
-n 4 (run 3)        ->  2 failed, 10 passed
```

Fails every time under parallel workers, passes every time serially, and the FAILING SET VARIES
between runs — the signature of a race on a shared resource rather than an order dependency.

### The mechanism: two independent 4s that are the same 4

- `max_concurrent_gates` defaults to **4** (`docs/config.md:597`), and gate admission raises
  `GateCongestedError` at capacity.
- `make test` runs `PYTEST_WORKERS ?= 4` (`Makefile:60`), and CI pins xdist `-n` to the
  runner's real vCPU count — **`ubuntu-latest = 4`** (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:789-790`).

Four xdist workers, four gate slots. When four gate-exercising tests land on four workers at
once, the fourth is refused. The admission bound is host-wide and process-crossing, so the
suite's own parallelism is enough to exhaust it; another session holding a real gate (an agent
running `review-plan`) just makes it likelier.

### Why this matters beyond a noisy local run

**This can produce a spurious `Verified -1` on any change**, because the gating CI cell is the
same 4-worker shape. That is a false signal on a merge gate, and per AGENTS.md the response to
a flaky test is to root-cause it rather than `recheck` — which is only possible once the cause
is written down, hence this ticket.

### Discovered from

Bug `5c5c-5741-9b33-47fa` (the ACLI ceiling partition). No overlap: every one of these tests is
in the plan-review / completion-gate area and none references `fetch_paging`, `fetcher`,
`collect_partitioned` or `_ACLI_CEILING`. All twelve pass serially with that change applied.

### Suggested direction (still not investigated in depth)

These are unit tests asserting instrumentation, retry and sidecar behaviour; none of them needs
a real host-wide admission slot. Options, in rough order of preference: stub admission for
tests; give the tests an isolated semaphore; or mark the family with an `xdist_group` so they
never run concurrently (the suite already uses `--dist loadgroup` elsewhere). Setting
`max_concurrent_gates = 0` for the test session disables the bound entirely and would also work,
but it stops exercising the admission path at all, so it is the weakest option.

### Revised acceptance criteria

- [ ] The failure is reproduced deterministically — DONE above: `-n 4` fails, serial passes.
- [ ] All thirteen known tests pass under `-n 4` with a busy host.
- [ ] They no longer depend on host-wide gate admission capacity: they pass with all real slots
      held by another process.
- [ ] What each test actually asserts is still asserted — the fix must not be deleting,
      skipping, or `xfail`-ing them.
- [ ] The two `assert 11 == 2` retry-count tests are confirmed to be the same root cause and
      not a second, independent defect hiding behind it.
- [ ] A sweep for any other test that takes a real gate admission slot.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND — and re-recorded here because the original write was STRANDED in an agent's
diverged worktree store and never reached the shared tracker. I have independently verified each
of its three load-bearing facts against `origin/main` before recording.

## The mechanism: two independent 4s that are the same 4

    docs/config.md:597                  max_concurrent_gates = 4   ("0 = off (no env override)")
    Makefile:60                         PYTEST_WORKERS ?= 4
    _build-and-test.yml:779-780         "-n is PINNED to the runner's real vCPU count
                                         (ubuntu-latest = 4, macos arm = 3), NOT -n auto"

Four pytest-xdist workers against a four-slot gate-admission semaphore. When more than one worker
lands on a gate-touching test at the same moment, **the suite exhausts its own semaphore** and a
test fails with `GateCongestedError: all 4 concurrent slots busy` — having proven nothing about
the code.

## Reproduced, not inferred

An agent ran the 12 failing tests alone on an otherwise-idle host:

| mode | result |
|---|---|
| serial | **12 passed** |
| `-n 4` run 1 | 3 failed |
| `-n 4` run 2 | 4 failed |
| `-n 4` run 3 | 2 failed |

Passes every serial run, fails every parallel run, and the FAILING SET VARIES between runs — the
signature of a race on a shared resource rather than a defect in any one test. Ten of the twelve
raise `GateCongestedError` by name; two more (`test_cli_retry_*`, and one asserting `11 == 2`)
fail DOWNSTREAM of the same congestion without naming it, which is why a grep for the error
undercounts the blast radius.

## Why this is more than a local annoyance

**The gating CI cell has exactly this shape.** `ubuntu-latest` gives 4 vCPUs, `-n` is pinned to 4,
and `max_concurrent_gates` is 4 with no env override available to widen it per-lane. So this can
produce a **spurious `Verified -1` on any change**, attributing a host-concurrency artefact to the
patchset under test. That is the same class this session has been cataloguing all night — an
infrastructure condition wearing the costume of a verdict — except here it lands on the merge gate.

Note the macOS asymmetry: `macos arm = 3` workers against 4 slots cannot exhaust it, which is part
of why this reads as intermittent rather than deterministic.

## Bearing on the fix

The originally-filed shape (one unit test taking a host-wide slot) is real but too narrow. Thirteen
tests are now known to participate, and the trigger is ordinary parallel execution, not one badly
behaved test. Worth deciding whether:
- `max_concurrent_gates` should exceed the worker count (it has NO env override today, so a lane
  cannot widen it);
- gate-touching tests should be serialised via `xdist_group`, the mechanism `_build-and-test.yml:915`
  already uses elsewhere (`--dist loadgroup`);
- or the tests should not take a real host slot at all.

Whatever is chosen, preserve the refusal's honesty: it currently says, correctly, *"This is HOST
CONGESTION, not a review result — no verdict was produced and nothing about the ticket was
judged."* That distinction is the reason this was diagnosable at all.

## Provenance note

The agent that found this could not record it: its worktree's ticket-store clone had diverged from
`origin/tickets` (no shared history), so its last writes were REFUSED — loudly, which is why the
finding survived in its report rather than vanishing. The shared store is healthy and in sync; the
divergence is confined to that worktree clone. Filed separately.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CORRECTION to the root cause I recorded above — mine was the smaller half, and I am superseding it.

I wrote that the mechanism is four pytest-xdist workers against a four-slot semaphore, i.e. *the
suite exhausting its own gate admission*. That is true and reproducible, but it does not explain
the observation that actually matters: running the failing tests ALONE, on a host with no other
tests running, still produced 14 failures.

## The deeper fact: the four slots are HOST-GLOBAL

`gate_admission._slot_dir()` resolves to `store_root()/locks`, and `store_root()` resolves to
`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` or else `tempfile.gettempdir()` — **one directory shared by every worktree,
every session, and every rebar process on the machine.**

An agent listed the live holders during a failing run:

    gate-slot-0   PID 50765   /Users/joeoakhart/janitor-e54e-shims      rebar verify-completion
    gate-slot-1   PID 6229    /Users/joeoakhart/janitor-f773-cli        rebar review-plan
    gate-slot-2   PID 20256   /Users/joeoakhart/rebar                   (global rebar-dev build)
    gate-slot-3   PID 89566   /Users/joeoakhart/janitor-038d-config     rebar ...

All four held by OTHER SESSIONS running real 15-20 minute LLM gate operations. The agent's own
pytest worker count at that moment was **zero**. So the tests were not competing with other tests —
they were competing with production gate work that was not running any test at all.

Two consequences follow that my version missed:

1. **"Run it in isolation" does not isolate.** The slot directory is outside the test session's
   control, so a serial re-run on a quiet-looking box still fails if four gate ops are open
   elsewhere on the machine. That is why the agent's first isolation run showed 14 failures and
   would have read as a real defect.
2. **The gate fails closed WITHOUT WAITING.** A test needing a slot dies instantly rather than
   queueing, so there is no backpressure — the failure is immediate and total rather than slow.

## Demonstrated fix direction

Re-running the same tests with a private `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` (its own `locks/`, its own four
slots) gave **71 passed / 0 failed**. So pointing the test fixture at a per-session slot directory
resolves it without touching the production limit.

## Revised CI consequence

My earlier note said the gating cell can produce a spurious `Verified -1` because 4 xdist workers
meet 4 slots. Still true. But the sharper statement is: **these tests are red whenever four real
gate operations are in flight anywhere on the box, including in CI if a runner is ever shared.**
The trigger is not confined to the suite's own parallelism.

Recording this as a correction rather than an addition, because a reader who acts only on my
earlier comment would fix the worker/slot ratio and still have red tests.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
SCOPE NOTE on the correction above, so it is not read as broader than it is.

My third comment corrects the mechanism stated in my SECOND comment — "four pytest-xdist workers ... the suite exhausts its own semaphore" — and nothing else. It does NOT correct this ticket's overall framing.

My FIRST comment already framed the cause cross-session ("Four slots, more than four consumers", naming another session's worktree by name), and AC4 already asked for exactly the slot-holder inventory that the host-global finding supplies. So a reader should not conclude that this ticket was wrong about the shape of the problem; it was right, and the second comment narrowed it in a way the third undoes.

What the host-global finding genuinely ADDS, over what this ticket already said:
- the concrete code path (`gate_admission._slot_dir()` -> `store_root()/locks` -> `tempfile.gettempdir()`);
- the scale — 31 tests across 9 files, not the single test originally filed;
- why ordinary triage misleads: re-running in isolation does not isolate, because the slot directory is outside the test session's control.

Recording this because I asked an implementing agent to write "this supersedes 9c2e's mechanism" into its own ticket, and it declined on the grounds that the record did not support the claim. It re-read this ticket, told me to do the same, and was correct. I withdrew the request. The detailed follow-up is filed as `stuffed-energistic-ladybird` (`846b-4b51-0254-48fd`), linked `relates_to`, and is positioned as the ANSWER to AC4 rather than a correction of it — which is the accurate relationship.

compiled_state.description:
## What was observed

During a `make verify` run on 2026-09-05 (while several other agent sessions were active on
the same host), the full suite reported:

```
1 failed, 19449 passed, 72 skipped, 13 warnings in 3021.66s (0:50:21)
FAILED tests/unit/test_completion_wrapper_duration_instrumentation.py::
       test_verify_completion_partitions_attempt_without_changing_verdict
  - rebar.llm.errors.GateCongestedError: gate admission refused: all 4 concurrent slots busy
```

Re-run in isolation immediately afterwards, the same file passes: `7 passed in 97.62s`.

## Why this matters

This is a **unit** test, but its outcome depends on a **host-wide, cross-process** resource:
the gate admission semaphore's 4 concurrent slots. Any other session on the machine holding
gate slots — another agent running `review-plan` or a completion-gated close, which is the
normal state of this repo's workflow — can fail it. That makes it:

- **a false `Verified -1` generator** on a busy CI runner or a shared dev box, and
- **misleading**: the failure names gate congestion, so an author has to rule out their own
  change before concluding it was contention.

Per AGENTS.md this is a bug to root-cause rather than a `recheck` candidate, because the
failure mode is reproducible by construction (occupy all 4 slots, run the test) rather than
genuinely random.

## Discovered from

Found incidentally while verifying the fix for bug `5c5c-5741-9b33-47fa` (the ACLI ceiling
partition). It has **no overlap** with that change — the test file contains zero references to
`fetch_paging`, `fetcher`, `collect_partitioned` or `_ACLI_CEILING` — so it was reported rather
than worked around, and the change was pushed on the strength of the other 19,449 passes.

## Suggested direction (not yet investigated)

A unit test asserting instrumentation/partitioning behaviour should not need a real admission
slot. Either stub the admission control for this test, or give the test its own isolated
semaphore rather than the process-wide/host-wide one. Confirm the actual coupling before
choosing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The failure is reproduced deterministically by occupying all 4 gate admission slots and
      running the test, confirming the coupling rather than assuming it.
- [ ] The test no longer depends on host-wide gate admission capacity: it passes with all
      slots occupied by another process.
- [ ] Whatever it was actually asserting (that `verify_completion` partitions the attempt
      without changing the verdict) is still asserted — the fix must not be deleting or
      skipping the assertion.
- [ ] A check that no other test in the suite has the same host-wide coupling, or a ticket
      filed for any that do.
compiled_state.title: Gate-admission tests race their own xdist workers: 12 unit tests fail with GateCongestedError under PYTEST_WORKERS=4, which equals max_concurrent_gates=4
